snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Unit 9 Hook: TNeGA: Nodal. Uzhavan: Agri. Naan Mudhalvan: Skills. e-Sevai: Certificates. Digital TN: Top. TVA: Culture.

quick_notes.title: TNeGA
quick_notes.detail: Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency. State nodal agency for all IT initiatives. Mission : "Service to People through Technology".
quick_notes.explanation: TNeGA stands for Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency. e-Governance means using computers and the internet to deliver government services to citizens more efficiently. TNeGA is the state nodal agency, which means it is the main coordinating body responsible for all information technology (IT) related projects and initiatives in the state of Tamil Nadu. Its official mission is "Service to People through Technology," meaning its goal is to make government services easier, faster, and more accessible by using digital tools. This agency helps other government departments adopt technology so that citizens can apply for certificates, pay bills, or access information online instead of visiting offices.

quick_notes.title: e-Sevai Centers
quick_notes.detail: Common Service Centers (CSC). Providing 100+ services like Community, Nativity, and Income certificates online.
quick_notes.explanation: TITLE: e-Sevai Centers e-Sevai Centers are government-run computer kiosks, also called Common Service Centers or CSCs, that provide over one hundred different services to the public through the internet. These centers allow you to apply for important documents like a Community Certificate, which proves your caste or community group, a Nativity Certificate, which proves you were born in a specific state or region, and an Income Certificate, which shows your family's yearly earnings. Instead of visiting a crowded government office, you can go to an e-Sevai Center, fill out an online form, and submit your application there. The center staff will help you with the process and print the certificate for you once it is approved by the government. This system makes getting official documents faster and easier, especially for people who do not have internet access at home.

quick_notes.title: Important Portals
quick_notes.detail: 1. Uzhavan App (Agriculture). 2. TN-SMART (Disaster management). 3. Naan Mudhalvan (Skill development). 4. e-Paarvai (Eye care).
quick_notes.explanation: The Uzhavan App is a mobile application created by the Tamil Nadu government to help farmers with agriculture-related information and services. TN-SMART stands for Tamil Nadu - System for Multi-Agency Response and Tracking, which is a digital platform used for disaster management, meaning it helps coordinate rescue and relief efforts during emergencies like floods or cyclones. Naan Mudhalvan, which means "I am the first" in Tamil, is a skill development program that offers online courses and training to help students and job seekers improve their abilities and find employment. e-Paarvai is an online system for eye care that allows people to register for free eye check-ups and treatments, especially in rural areas.

quick_notes.title: Tamil Virtual Academy (TVA)
quick_notes.detail: Providing internet-based resources for Tamil language and culture globally. Digital library of Tamil literature.
quick_notes.explanation: Tamil Virtual Academy (TVA) is a government organization established by the Tamil Nadu government to spread Tamil language and culture around the world using the internet. It offers a free digital library where you can read thousands of Tamil books, poems, and ancient texts online without needing to visit a physical library. TVA also provides online courses to teach Tamil to people who live outside Tamil Nadu or in other countries. These courses are designed for beginners, children, and advanced learners, and they include lessons on grammar, literature, and spoken Tamil. The academy creates and hosts digital resources like dictionaries, encyclopedias, and audio recordings to help anyone, anywhere, learn about Tamil heritage. In short, TVA's main goal is to make Tamil language and culture accessible to everyone through the internet.

quick_notes.title: State Data Center (SDC)
quick_notes.detail: Secure infrastructure for hosting state government applications and data.
quick_notes.explanation: TITLE: State Data Center (SDC) A State Data Center, or SDC, is a secure physical building filled with computers and storage equipment that the state government uses to run its online services and keep its official records. Think of it as a very safe, high-tech library where all the digital files and programs for things like issuing driver's licenses or managing land records are stored and made available to citizens. The word "secure" means the building has strong locks, cameras, and backup power to protect the data from theft, fire, or power cuts. "Hosting" means the SDC provides the space, electricity, and internet connection so that government applications (like a website to pay property tax) can work properly without crashing. This center is different from a normal office computer because it is built to run 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and can handle thousands of people using it at the same time. In short, the SDC is the state government's main, protected computer room that makes sure all its digital services are always available and safe.
